title: Barrie prisoner dies in hospital after arrest
subtitle: A Barrie man has died after being briefly held in a city jail cell Saturday night.
article: A Barrie man has died after being briefly held in a city jail cell Saturday night.
Jason Snow, 38, was pronounced dead at Royal Victoria Hospital in Barrie on Tuesday, the province's Special Investigations Unit announced on Thursday.
Snow was hospitalized after he went into distress in a jail cell following his arrest for public intoxication.
The SIU has assigned three investigators to probe what happened to Snow.
A post mortem examination is scheduled for Friday.
According to the SIU, Snow was arrested at 6.30 pm on Saturday at the city's bus depot.
At 11 p.m. on Saturday, Snow was transported to the Royal Victoria Hospital, where he was placed on life support.
"He was a helluva guy," Martin Bosma of Barrie said. "He was my best friend."
Bosma said he knew few details of his friend's death.
Snow, who was single, worked as a landscaper for 10 years for Jim Jennings of Bradford.
"He was a good hard worker," Jennings said. "He was liked by a lot of people. I always thought he had a lot of potential."
Friends said that Snow was raised with his three siblings by his single mother, and that he started to drink heavily after her death a year ago.
"He was very close to her," said family friend Bill Skwarchuk of Bradford.
"That was the start of it (his health) going really bad," Jennings said.
A spokesperson for the SIU said the agency was contacted by Barrie police Sunday.
The SIU are responsible for investigating police when there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault in incidents involving police.
Investigators include an officer who specializes in forensic evidence, according to SIU spokesperson Frank Phillips.
